reason: Both CIFs parse, symmetry-expand at full occupancy to primitive 14-atom Pmc2_1 cells (Sr4Hf2Te8, Z = 2; 4.04396 x 12.40953 x 7.29275 A), and they are genuinely distinct coordinate realizations rather than settings or supercells. The orthorhombic metric has strong line coverage (71/72 prominence > 2 peaks used in the trace; only weak residual features remain), but the atomic model is not established. The instantiated whole-profile residuals are 0.1935 for selected.cif and 0.5841 for alternative-1.cif, versus an independently audited Pmc2_1 Pawley-like intensity lower bound of about 0.078 (estimated noise-only scale about 0.024). The selected CIF also misses decisive low-angle intensity ratios (for example observed normalized intensities at 14.07, 18.76, 24.73, and 26.17 degrees are about 100, 3.9, 20.9, and 55.4, while its instantiated CIF gives about 59.8, 19.0, 13.3, and 23.6) and has implausible Hf-Te contacts of 2.47-2.61 A plus Sr-Hf contacts near 2.59 A; its Hf bond-valence sum is about 7.1 rather than +4. The chemically more regular alternative improves the Hf shell but is the much poorer profile model, so the trace's claim that it is homometric is quantitatively false. No independently convergent coordinate solution reconciles these constraints, making another attempt likely to add a materially different viable realization in the indexed cell.
